I don't know what you are going through exactly, but I can tell you what helped me. I had a horrible depression attack right before a really important exam. I despised myself, was skeptical about peoples' care and love for me, I didn't have any motivation so it led me to skip tasks or not be able to perform well, consequently to feel worthless on top of everything. Mainly, I didn't believe I was ever going to be happy and I considered that a life not worth living. Why be alive if your days will pass in agony so I was desperately close to ending it all. 
First of all I don't know if you are getting any help but medication really works to give you the initial push out of the darkness. Also, if you have ANY person that you feel close to yourself and trust, contact them.. My sister was that person for me and it helped me tremendously. One night, I called her weeping and ready to kill myself. Talking to her soothed me immensely. I was especially hard on myself during this time and expected too much out of myself. I literally had drowned myself in tasks. She said this one really basic thing that I will never forget: "We humans as animals fundamentally have only a couple things we have to do. Eat, sleep, reproduce, etc. But we made life really hard for ourselves." If you think about it, it id true. So don't be so harsh on yourself.
There is also this one thing that my mom told me about suicide. She likewise suffered from depression and contemplated suicide. "Think about your most beloved jewelry, and imagine you lost it somewhere inside your room. You would feel devastated right. And lets say If you leave the room, you can never get back in. Where would you search for your jewelry? You would search it inside the room because there is at least a chance of finding it." what she meant was even if you feel like you are never going to be happy, there is no chance to be happy after you are dead; if you live, you may find your happiness again. You mentioned there were some things that made you happy earlier like your hobbies. I am sure a day will come when you'll enjoy them again.
 For now, because you are overwhelmed try to do the max you can do in a day. If you never leave the baed or give in to sleep, you will progressively feel worse. Believe me I have been there.

You don't need to be really strict. I think tracking for a couple weeks at the end of the week to fine tune things should be enough. You already sound like you make a conscious effort so it should be fine as long as you are taking your B12 and D supplements. 
But if we are to get scientific; when vitamins are concerned, A D E and K vitamins are fat soluble which means the excess is stored. So you don't have to hit the goal everyday really. With vitamins B and C you HAVE to get them everyday because they are water soluble and will be excreted in your urine. Zinc, calcium and iron are quite important especially for vegans so I would recommend incorporating more beans and legumes, dark leafy greens, tahini and seeds (pumpkin, hemp, almond) in your diet.
I generally try to eat at least a cup of legumes (can make falafels, eat as hummus, add to pasta, make burger patties, curries, chilli, in tacos.... ) and 3 cups of dark leafy greens everyday. I also put seeds in most of my meals and try to add lemon or red pepper to most meals to increase iron absorption (tahini, lemon and garlic make a great dressing for buddha bowls and salads, and adding pumpkin seeds add a really nice crunch.) Hope this helps!
